report.purpose: Measure retrieval of developers associated with held-out expertise evidence.
report.interpretation_boundary: The benchmark does not prove universal developer expertise, identify the best developer, or establish universal recommender superiority.

benchmark_statistics.held_out_selection: Deterministically highest comment ID among supported reviewer-category evidence.

multi_category_metrics.exact_definition: Retrieved held-out developer has every requested category in held-out labels.
multi_category_metrics.partial_definition: Retrieved held-out developer has at least one requested category in held-out labels.

checks: held-out IDs excluded from profile supporting evidence
profile evidence exclusion recorded per query
relevance labels independent of recommendation output

reproducibility.tie_breaking: recommendation score descending, matched-category count descending, gold count descending, username ascending
reproducibility.software_environment: Python 3.11 executable used for validation; pytest 9.1.1 installed during the prior validation session

warnings.message: unknown classes TESTING_QUALITY, DATA_MANAGEMENT, and/or PERF_OPTIMIZATION were ignored in cross-validation folds
warnings.effect: test-data fold warning; no benchmark artifact or recommendation result is changed
warnings.follow_up: Review fold construction if cross-validation diagnostics are expanded; not a Phase 7B validity failure.

warnings.message: Number of distinct clusters (2) found smaller than n_clusters (3)
warnings.effect: exploratory clustering warning caused by duplicate test points; unrelated to benchmark retrieval metrics
warnings.follow_up: Use a less duplicated fixture or adjust exploratory test cluster count if that test is maintained.

limitations: 142 held-out queries are sufficient for descriptive reporting but small for multi-category and some category-level slices.
Category support is uneven: single-category support ranges from 4 to 18 queries.
The corpus covers 10 selected repositories and 1,225 review comments, not all developer activity.
Relevance represents held-out labeled review evidence, not complete or universal capability.
Natural-language evaluation uses deterministic taxonomy mapping and separately audits mapping behavior.
Bot/service identities are excluded from human recommendation evaluation, so results describe the human candidate population only.
Classifier predictions are confidence-tiered decision-margin outputs, not calibrated probabilities.
Only six multi-category queries were supported by the held-out evidence protocol.
